co_rough_canyon.blurb: Rough Canyon is a quiet, lightly developed canyon just south of Grand Junction, reached from the Little Park Road side of town. Most of the fifteen climbs here are traditional lines, with a single sport route and one aid line mixed in. Grades run from easy fifth class through the 5.9 range, with a cluster of 5.11 routes and one 5.12 near the top end. Its best-known feature is Tabeguache Tower, a free-standing spire. The cliffs are scattered rather than packed into one wall, so expect some exploring and a short scramble in, and a quiet day with few other parties. Midday sun can be strong, so cooler hours suit it best.

co_sanctuary_the_2.blurb: The Sanctuary is the farthest-up of the named boulder groups at Big Elk Meadows, in the St. Vrain canyons near Lyons. Expect around fifteen problems, mostly vertical or just off vertical rather than steep, with a couple of top-ropes. They range from easy V0 and V1 cracks and arete lines through the middle grades to a handful of V8 testpieces, with straight-up edge problems and a long traverse in between. The boulders are solid and sometimes large, with flat landings but fairly high top-outs, so a pad or two is worth carrying. The walk in follows the creek and takes roughly twenty minutes or more.

co_south_formation.blurb: South Formation is one of the two granite domes at Button Rock, on a ridge above Pinewood Springs near Lyons. The rock stands over 160 feet tall and mixes face, crack, slab and roof climbing. Fifteen routes are recorded, split between traditional lines and bolted sport pitches, and grades are on the hard side: a few in the 5.7 to 5.10 range, then a strong group at 5.12 and a couple of 5.13s. The walk up is steep, taking about half an hour to the saddle, and some cracks are dirty and lichen-covered, so it rewards experienced parties. The west face catches warm afternoon sun.

co_stripe_the.blurb: The Stripe is a small sport crag in the Animas River canyon just below Silverton, at roughly 9,300 feet. Nearly all of its fifteen routes are bolted, with a single trad line, and they stay at or under about 90 feet. The grades are friendly for a mountain crag: a couple of 5.7 and 5.8 warm-ups on the left, a solid core of 5.10s, and a few harder pitches up to the low 5.13 range on the upper tier. There is next to no approach, apart from a scramble up the left side to reach the upper tier, which makes it an easy half-day stop.

co_whirlpool_rock.blurb: Whirlpool Rock is a steep granite cliff on Independence Pass, a short uphill walk above a roadside pool on the Aspen side. It is mostly a trad cliff where gear is hard to find, so it lacks the bolt ladders common elsewhere, with a few sport and top-rope lines and several boulder problems in the talus below. Fifteen climbs span roughly V1 to V7 for boulders and 5.8 to 5.12 on rope, with the 5.10s and 5.11s making up the core. Route-finding is funky and the angle is sustained, so it suits confident leaders. Start early to avoid afternoon storms common at this altitude.

co_warm_up_boulder_12.blurb: Warm-up Boulder is a freestanding block among the 420s boulders in Poudre Canyon, west of Rustic and north of Fort Collins, in a subalpine setting at about 9,400 feet. It gives around fifteen problems on its different faces, and the spread is gentle at the bottom: a good number of V1 and V2 lines, a few V3 and V4s, then a handful of harder problems including traverses up to V8. That mix makes it a natural first stop before moving on to the rest of the area's Camp 4 style boulders. Summer is the time to go, when the high setting stays cool.

co_scorpio_crag.blurb: Scorpio Crag is the main roped crag in Picket Wire Canyon, in the Comanche National Grassland south of La Junta. Fifteen short routes on varnished sandstone cliffs of around 30 to 50 feet offer face climbing and varied cracks, split among trad, sport and top-rope lines. Grades start at easy fifth class and cluster in the 5.7 to 5.10 range, with a few 5.11s and one 5.12 on top. The rock looks chossy but climbs better than it appears. It is a remote, high-desert spot, with much of the surrounding cliff line still undeveloped, so bring water and plan for a quiet day.
